controls.question: ISMS aligned to ISO 27001 / NIST CSF
controls.evidence: No formal ISMS today. Hosting platforms (Supabase, Netlify, GitHub) hold their own certifications, but those do not cover Clicka's own management system.
controls.gap: Write a short ISMS: scope, risk register, policy set (access, acceptable use, data, incident, BC/DR, supplier, SDLC), mapped to NIST CSF. Management sign-off, review every 6–12 months.

controls.question: Dedicated Information Security Officer or equivalent
controls.evidence: No named role. Technical decisions sit with Warren, operations with Philip.
controls.gap: Appoint a named Information Security Officer in writing (can be a part-time role), with a deputy. Record the appointment and board/director sign-off.

controls.question: Regular independent / self assessments (ISO 27001/2, NIST CSF)
controls.evidence: This FNB assessment is the first formal one. A Supabase security-advisor review was done earlier.
controls.gap: Run a NIST CSF self-assessment now, repeat every 6 months, and book an independent pen test / review (see Q19). Keep the reports.

controls.question: Comply with POPIA / GDPR / PCI DSS where applicable
controls.evidence: Trader consent and signature step at onboarding; marketing opt-in on rewards sign-up; no card numbers stored (Shop2Shop handles card/QR). No documented POPIA programme.
controls.gap: Appoint an Information Officer (POPIA requirement), register with the Information Regulator, write a POPIA compliance file (processing register, consent records, operator agreements). State clearly that Clicka holds no card data, so PCI DSS is out of scope.

controls.question: Privacy Policy and procedures for personal data
controls.evidence: Consent wording exists in the onboarding flow. CONFIRM whether a published privacy policy and data-subject request procedure exist.
controls.gap: Publish a privacy policy; add procedures for access, correction and deletion requests, breach notification and operator contracts. Add wording that covers sharing transaction data with the bank.

controls.question: Documented data retention and destruction policies
controls.evidence: No retention schedule. The switch ledger is deliberately append-only and holds references only, so personal data can be deleted elsewhere.
controls.gap: Write a retention schedule per data category (stores, owners, orders, payments, logs, ledger) with a deletion method and owner. Test one real deletion.

controls.question: Cross-border data transfers comply with regulations
controls.evidence: CONFIRM the Supabase and Netlify regions. Anything outside South Africa is a cross-border transfer under POPIA section 72.
controls.gap: Record the region of each database and bucket. If outside SA, document the legal basis (operator agreement, adequate protection) or move the data. FNB may require SA hosting for its data.

controls.question: Asset inventory (users, systems, devices, data, third parties)
controls.evidence: A high-level infrastructure note exists; no maintained inventory.
controls.gap: Build one register: systems and accounts (Supabase, Netlify, GitHub, domain, Shop2Shop), staff and role list, company devices, data stores, and third parties. Review quarterly.

controls.question: Classify and label data
controls.evidence: Ledger design keeps personal data out of events. No classification scheme.
controls.gap: Adopt a four-level scheme (public / internal / confidential / bank-restricted). Tag every table and bucket. Mark FNB-sourced data as bank-restricted and keep it server-side only.

controls.question: Protect data at rest and in transit
controls.evidence: TLS on all traffic; Supabase encrypts databases and storage at rest; secrets held as server environment variables, not in the browser. Strong, mostly inherited.
controls.gap: Document it with evidence (platform encryption statements, screenshots). Rotate secrets on a schedule; confirm no keys in repos. Keep as Managed.

controls.question: Encrypt portable devices
controls.evidence: CONFIRM disk encryption on every laptop that touches production. Field agents' phones carry the app but should hold no bank data.
controls.gap: Turn on BitLocker / device encryption on all company laptops, enforce screen lock, and record it in the asset register. Keep FNB data off phones. If no company device holds bank data, ask FNB whether this can be N/A.

controls.question: RBAC, least privilege, need-to-know
controls.evidence: Strong: staff roles with scopes, admin-only functions, brand scoping, row-level security with server-side service key, maker-checker planned for payments. Gap: the service key is powerful.
controls.gap: Document the role matrix (the Roles & Permissions document already exists), limit who holds the service key, keep a short list of exceptions. Show an access review.

controls.question: MFA for all users, privileged and remote access
controls.evidence: Admin login is email and password. Supabase supports MFA but it is not enforced. Trader device PIN is a second factor only for traders. CONFIRM MFA on Supabase, Netlify, GitHub and email accounts.
controls.gap: Enforce MFA on: Supabase, Netlify, GitHub, domain registrar, email, and the Clicka Admin login (add authenticator-app MFA for all staff, mandatory for Admin and payment roles).

controls.question: Automated IAM with lifecycle, attestation and governance
controls.evidence: Staff are created, scoped, deactivated and password-reset inside Clicka Admin, with status flags. No periodic attestation and no joiner/leaver checklist.
controls.gap: Add a joiner-mover-leaver procedure, a quarterly access review that is signed off and stored, and an admin-action audit log. Together this is a credible Defined-to-Managed position.

controls.question: Network segmentation for sensitive systems
controls.evidence: Clicka is ring-fenced from every other entity (own Supabase org, repo, Netlify). Bank-facing functions can be separated. Serverless, so no traditional network.
controls.gap: Keep the 3PIM connector in its own server functions with its own secrets, and document the architecture and trust boundaries in a diagram.

controls.question: Firewalls and IDS/IPS, actively monitored
controls.evidence: Platform-level DDoS and edge protection from Netlify and Supabase, but no monitored IDS and no alerts.
controls.gap: Turn on platform firewall/rate-limit rules, alerting on auth failures and error spikes, and name who receives the alerts. Cover with the managed monitoring in Q22.

controls.question: No unsupported OS, database, hardware or software
controls.evidence: Modern managed stack (Node 22, current Postgres via Supabase). CONFIRM the Android wrapper build tools and staff laptops are on supported versions.
controls.gap: Record versions in the asset register and check them each quarter.

controls.question: Patching to industry best practice
controls.evidence: Platform patching is handled by the providers. Dependencies are not tracked on a schedule.
controls.gap: Turn on Dependabot or similar for all repos, set patch timelines (critical in days, others monthly), and keep a patch log.

controls.question: Continuous vulnerability scanning and penetration testing
controls.evidence: Supabase security advisor was run and exposure fixed. No scanner, no pen test.
controls.gap: Commission an external penetration test of the Admin app, ordering app and the payments functions; add automated dependency, secret and web scanning in the pipeline; fix and re-test findings.

controls.question: Secure SDLC and secure coding practices
controls.evidence: Code is syntax-checked and tested on live data. Server functions check roles. No branch protection, mandatory review, or security testing documented.
controls.gap: Write a secure SDLC standard: branch protection and required review on main, secret scanning, SAST, a security checklist per change, change log. This single question carries a full domain, so it must reach Managed (4).

controls.question: Physical access and acceptable-use procedures
controls.evidence: Remote/cloud operation. Data-centre security is inherited from the cloud providers. No Clicka acceptable-use or clean-desk policy.
controls.gap: Write an acceptable-use and remote-work standard (screen lock, clean desk, no shared devices, no data on paper) and attach the providers' SOC 2 / ISO reports for data-centre controls. Ask FNB in writing whether Not Applicable is acceptable for a no-premises company; do not self-declare it.

controls.question: SOC with a SIEM
controls.evidence: No SOC or SIEM. Platform logs exist.
controls.gap: Contract a low-cost managed detection and response / SIEM service, or ship Supabase, Netlify and application logs into one monitored log tool with alert rules and an on-call name.

controls.question: Security logs retained and reviewed
controls.evidence: Platform logs are kept. The payments ledger is hash-chained and tamper-evident, with a chain-verify function.
controls.gap: Set retention (12 months), schedule a weekly log review with a signed note, log admin actions and logins to a central place. Show the ledger verify run as evidence.

controls.question: Threat intelligence, threat hunting, external and insider threat monitoring
controls.evidence: Not in place and not planned.
controls.gap: Get this through the managed service in Q22 (it normally includes threat feeds and hunting). Add insider-threat controls: least privilege, action logging, maker-checker on payments.

controls.question: Documented incident response plan, regularly tested
controls.evidence: No plan.
controls.gap: Write an incident response plan (roles, severity levels, bank and regulator notification timelines, breach register), then hold a tabletop exercise and keep the minutes. Repeat twice a year.

controls.question: DR and BCP with RTO/RPO, tested regularly
controls.evidence: Provider backups, git history and atomic deploys give rollback. No RTO/RPO, no documented plan, no restore test. Single-question domain, so it must reach 4.
controls.gap: Set RTO/RPO, confirm backup frequency and retention (consider point-in-time recovery), write the BCP/DR plan, and do a real restore test with a dated report. Repeat every 6 months.

controls.question: Assess suppliers' and subcontractors' security
controls.evidence: Relies on certified platforms. No documented supplier review.
controls.gap: Keep a supplier register and collect each provider's SOC 2 / ISO certificate (Supabase, Netlify, GitHub, Shop2Shop, WhatsApp/SMS providers). Review annually and record risk.

controls.question: Security requirements in third-party contracts
controls.evidence: CONFIRM what the Shop2Shop and other agreements say about security and data protection.
controls.gap: Add a standard security and POPIA operator schedule to supplier and partner contracts, and check existing ones.

controls.question: Annual security awareness training
controls.evidence: Role-based app training decks exist, but not security awareness.
controls.gap: Run annual security awareness training for all staff and agents who touch data; keep attendance records. Add induction training for new joiners.

controls.question: Phishing simulations / social engineering campaigns
controls.evidence: None.
controls.gap: Use a phishing-simulation service for staff, quarterly, with results reported. Add a short social-engineering briefing for field staff.

policies.title: ISMS Policy
policies.summary: Part A: information security management system covering scope, roles, risk, the 11 control domains and incident reporting.
policies.body_md:
# Part A: ISMS Policy

## 1. Purpose

Clicka Technologies (Pty) Ltd (Clicka) is a first-party data and commerce platform for South Africa's informal trade economy. Clicka also connects to bank payment infrastructure (FNB / RMB 3PIM) as a Trusted Partner. This policy sets out how Clicka protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of its systems and data, including data received from FirstRand, trader and merchant personal information, and brand-licensed data.

## 2. Scope

This ISMS covers every system, person and process involved in operating the Clicka platform:

- Production systems: the Clicka Supabase project (database, authentication, storage), Netlify sites and serverless functions, GitHub repositories, and the domain and DNS.
- Applications: Clicka Admin, the Spaza Onboard / ordering app (web and Android), Clicka BI and Trade Map, the payment and switching functions, and the Shop2Shop listener.
- People: directors, employees, contractors (including developers) and field staff such as agents, PPM agents and drivers.
- Devices: all laptops and phones used to access production systems or Clicka data.
- Data: all personal, commercial and bank-sourced data held or processed by Clicka.
Bank-restricted data rule: data that originates from FirstRand / 3PIM (account details, balances, transaction history, payment instructions and responses) is processed only inside Clicka's server-side environment. It is never returned to, stored on, or displayed on field-staff phones or in any browser session other than authorised, MFA-protected administrator roles. Field apps show only an order's paid / unpaid status.

## 3. Roles and responsibilities


| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Directors | Approve this policy and resources; receive a security report at least twice a year; accept residual risk in writing. |
| Information Security Officer (ISO) | Owns the ISMS; runs risk assessments, reviews and audits; keeps the policy set current; reports to the directors; first point of contact for FNB / 3PIM on security. [Appoint in writing; name a deputy.] |
| Information Officer (POPIA) | Registered with the Information Regulator; owns personal-information compliance, data-subject requests and breach notification. [May be the same person as the ISO, but record both appointments.] |
| Technical Lead | Owns secure design, access to production, change control, backups, monitoring and vulnerability management. |
| All staff and contractors | Follow the Acceptable Use Policy, complete training, report incidents immediately. |

## 4. Risk management

1. Maintain a risk register covering assets, threats, likelihood, impact, owner, controls and treatment (reduce, transfer, accept, avoid).
1. Review the register at least every six months and whenever the platform changes materially (for example when the 3PIM connector goes live).
1. Assess every new supplier or integration before it receives Clicka or bank data (see Part C).
1. Run a self-assessment against the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FNB Trusted Partner questionnaire every six months, and commission an independent review or penetration test at least annually.
## 5. Control framework

Controls are organised under the eleven FNB assessment domains. Each control has an owner and produces evidence that is kept for review.


| Domain | Minimum standard | Evidence kept |
|---|---|---|
| Governance | This ISMS, named ISO, six-monthly self-assessment, annual independent assessment. | Signed policy, appointment letter, assessment reports |
| Legal and regulatory | POPIA compliance file: processing register, consent records, operator agreements, privacy policy, retention schedule, cross-border transfer record, data-subject request log. | Compliance file, Regulator registration, request log |
| Asset and data management | Single asset register (systems, accounts, people, devices, data stores, suppliers); four data classes (Public, Internal, Confidential, Bank-restricted); encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest; encrypted devices. | Asset register, classification tags, encryption statements, device checks |
| Access control and identity | Role-based, least-privilege access; MFA on all staff and administrator access and on every production, code and email account; quarterly access review; joiner-mover-leaver procedure; service keys restricted and rotated. | Role matrix, MFA settings, access review sign-offs, leaver checklists |
| Network and infrastructure | Segmented environments (payments functions isolated); platform firewall and rate limiting; supported software only; patching within set timelines; vulnerability scanning and annual penetration test. | Architecture diagram, patch log, scan and test reports |
| Application security | Secure development standard: protected main branch, peer review, secret and dependency scanning, security checklist per change, no secrets in code, separate test and production data. | Pull-request history, scan results, change log |
| Physical security | Cloud-only operation; data-centre controls inherited from certified providers; remote-work and clean-desk standard (Part B). | Provider SOC 2 / ISO certificates, signed acceptable-use acknowledgements |
| Monitoring and incident response | Central logging of authentication, administrator and payment events; alerts to a named person; log retention of 12 months; weekly log review; tested incident response plan. | Alert rules, weekly review notes, incident register, tabletop minutes |
| Business continuity and DR | Documented RTO and RPO; automated backups with point-in-time recovery where available; restore tested every six months; rollback procedure for deployments. | BC/DR plan, restore-test reports |
| Vendor and supply chain | Supplier register, risk tiering, evidence review and security schedule in contracts (Part C). | Register, certificates, signed schedules |
| Training and awareness | Security and POPIA training at induction and annually; phishing simulations at least quarterly; social-engineering briefing for field staff. | Attendance records, simulation results |

## 6. Supporting policies (to be written under this ISMS)

- Access Control Policy and role matrix
- Data Classification, Retention and Destruction Policy
- Incident Response Plan and breach register (includes bank and Regulator notification timelines)
- Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan
- Secure Development and Change Control Standard
- Privacy Policy and Data-Subject Request Procedure
- Cryptography and Secrets Management Standard
## 7. Incident reporting

Anyone who suspects a security incident, lost device, suspicious message or data exposure must report it to the ISO immediately and no later than the same working day. The ISO logs the incident, contains it, and decides on notification to FNB / 3PIM, the Information Regulator and affected parties within the periods set by the Incident Response Plan, the Data Feed Agreement and POPIA.

## 8. Exceptions, compliance and review

Exceptions must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, approved by the ISO and a director, time-limited, and recorded in the exceptions register. Breaches of this policy may lead to disciplinary action or termination of contracts. The ISO reviews this policy at least every 12 months and presents results to the directors.

policies.title: Acceptable Use Policy
policies.summary: Part B: accounts and MFA, devices, remote work, data handling, AI tools and prohibited use.
policies.body_md:
# Part B: Acceptable Use Policy

This policy applies to everyone who uses Clicka systems, data or devices: directors, employees, contractors and field staff. Acknowledgement is required at induction and annually.

## 1. General rules

- Use Clicka systems and data only for Clicka business and only as far as your role requires.
- Never share your login, PIN, password or authenticator device. Everything done under your account is treated as done by you.
- Keep personal and bank-sourced data inside approved systems. Do not copy it to personal email, messaging apps, personal cloud storage or removable media.
- Report anything suspicious straight away. Reporting a mistake early is always better than hiding it.
## 2. Accounts, passwords and MFA

- Multi-factor authentication is mandatory on all Clicka Admin, Supabase, Netlify, GitHub, domain registrar and company email accounts.
- Use a company-approved password manager. Passwords must be unique, at least 14 characters (or a long passphrase), and never reused across services.
- Trader and agent device PINs must not be shared and are locked after repeated wrong attempts.
- Administrator and developer accounts are separate from everyday accounts where the platform allows.
## 3. Devices

- Company laptops must have full-disk encryption (for example BitLocker), automatic screen lock within five minutes, an up-to-date operating system and antivirus or endpoint protection.
- Personal phones used by field staff may run the Clicka app but must have a screen lock. They must never hold bank-sourced data, exports of merchant lists, screenshots of payment details or administrator sessions.
- Lost or stolen devices must be reported at once so access can be revoked.
- Do not install unapproved software on devices used for production access.
## 4. Remote work, clean desk and physical security

- Clicka operates remotely and in the field. Work only in places where screens cannot be read by others; lock the screen whenever you step away.
- Do not leave devices unattended in vehicles or public places. Do not use shared or public computers for Clicka accounts.
- Keep no printed copies of merchant, payment or credential data; if unavoidable, store securely and shred after use.
- Use trusted networks. On public Wi-Fi use a mobile hotspot or VPN.
## 5. Data handling

- Handle data according to its class: Public, Internal, Confidential (personal and commercial data), Bank-restricted (FirstRand / 3PIM data).
- Bank-restricted data stays on the server side and is viewed only by authorised administrators. It is never sent by chat or email and never shown in field apps.
- Share brand or merchant data only through approved Clicka reports, licensed products and the MCP connector, with consent and agreements in place. Identifiable merchant data is never sold or shared outside those arrangements.
- Delete or return data when the purpose ends, following the retention schedule.
## 6. Software and AI tools

- Use only approved development and productivity tools. Do not paste secrets, personal data or bank-sourced data into any external tool, chat or AI service that is not approved for that data.
- Code changes to production go through the change process: pull request, review, merge to the protected main branch. Never commit secrets or keys to a repository.
## 7. Prohibited activities

- Attempting to access data or systems beyond your role, or to bypass security controls.
- Scanning, testing or attacking Clicka or third-party systems without written authority.
- Installing malware, cracking tools or unlicensed software.
- Using Clicka systems for unlawful, harassing, discriminatory or personal commercial activity.
- Taking photographs or recordings of screens that show confidential or bank-restricted data.
## 8. Monitoring, breaches and consequences

Clicka logs authentication, administrator and payment activity to protect the platform and meet bank requirements. Use of company systems may be monitored in line with POPIA and employment law. Breaches of this policy may result in disciplinary action, termination of contracts and, where the law is broken, reporting to authorities.

## 9. Acknowledgement


| Name | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |

policies.title: Supplier Security Review
policies.summary: Part C: risk tiers, procedure, questionnaire, contract clauses and the supplier register.
policies.body_md:
# Part C: Supplier Security Review

## 1. Purpose and scope

This procedure makes sure every supplier, subcontractor or integration partner that handles Clicka systems or data is assessed before onboarding, reviewed at least annually, and bound by contract to appropriate security and privacy terms. It answers FNB questions 27 and 28.

## 2. Risk tiers


| Tier | Definition | Minimum review |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Hosts or processes production data, or connects to the bank or payment rails. | Certificate review (SOC 2 / ISO 27001), completed questionnaire, contract security schedule, annual reassessment, exit plan |
| High | Handles personal or commercial data or is a dependency for core operations. | Certificate or questionnaire, contract schedule, annual review |
| Standard | Limited or no access to data. | Basic due-diligence check and terms review at onboarding, review every two years |

## 3. Procedure

1. Business owner raises a request describing the supplier, what data they will touch and why.
1. ISO assigns a risk tier and sends the supplier questionnaire (below) and asks for current certificates and the latest audit report.
1. ISO reviews the evidence, records findings and any conditions in the supplier register, and decides: approve, approve with conditions, or decline.
1. Legal confirms the contract includes the security and POPIA schedule (section 5). Critical suppliers must also have a data processing (operator) agreement.
1. Access is granted at least privilege and recorded in the asset register.
1. Review annually (Critical and High), or sooner after an incident, a change of ownership or a major service change. Revoke access and recover data at termination.
## 4. Supplier questionnaire (minimum)

- Do you hold a current ISO 27001 certificate or SOC 2 Type II report? Please attach it.
- Where is our data stored and processed (country and region)? Do you transfer it across borders?
- How is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
- Do you enforce MFA for staff, and how is staff access to customer data controlled and logged?
- How do you manage vulnerabilities and patching, and when was your last independent penetration test?
- What is your incident notification commitment (time to tell us of a breach)?
- What are your backup, recovery (RTO/RPO) and continuity arrangements?
- Which sub-processors do you use?
- How do you return or delete our data on termination?
## 5. Contract security and POPIA schedule (required clauses)

- Confidentiality and use of data only for the agreed purpose.
- Security measures at least equal to recognised standards (ISO 27001 / SOC 2).
- Breach notification to Clicka without undue delay and within a stated period.
- Right to request evidence and to audit, or to receive independent reports.
- Sub-processor approval and flow-down of the same terms.
- Data location and cross-border transfer limits, and return or deletion on termination.
- POPIA operator terms where personal information is processed.
## 6. Supplier register (opening position)

*Initial population from what is known about the platform. Items marked CONFIRM need a document or answer from the supplier before the review is complete.*


| Supplier | Service / data | Tier | Evidence to collect | Contract status | Next review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supabase | Database, authentication, storage (all Clicka production data) | Critical | SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, region (CONFIRM), DPA | CONFIRM DPA signed | [date] |
| Netlify | Hosting, serverless functions, environment secrets | Critical | SOC 2 report, DPA, data location | CONFIRM DPA | [date] |
| GitHub | Source code and change control | High | SOC 2 / ISO report; confirm no secrets in repos | Standard terms | [date] |
| Shop2Shop (and Simple POS) | Wallet payments, RabbitMQ payment notifications, POS integration | Critical | Security documentation, UAT and production access terms, data processing terms | CONFIRM security clauses | [date] |
| FNB / RMB (3PIM) | Bank connectivity, account and transaction data, payments | Critical | Trusted Partner agreement, Data Feed Agreement, API terms | In negotiation | [date] |
| Domain / DNS provider | clicka.co.za domain and DNS | High | MFA, registrar lock, contact details | CONFIRM | [date] |
| Email and messaging (WhatsApp / SMS provider) | Customer and staff communication | High | Provider certifications, data location (CONFIRM provider) | CONFIRM | [date] |
| Listener host (to be chosen) | Always-on worker for Shop2Shop messages | Critical | SOC 2 / ISO, region, secrets handling | Not yet contracted | [date] |
| Developers and contractors | Code and platform build | High | NDA, security and POPIA schedule, MFA and device standard | CONFIRM | [date] |
| AI-assisted development tools | Code assistance (no production or bank data to be shared) | High | Approved-use rules, data-retention terms | CONFIRM | [date] |

Once the register is complete, attach each supplier's certificate or report and record the reviewer and date. This register plus the evidence is what Clicka shows FNB for questions 27 and 28.
